query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a Cr-rich oxide layer through doping with 5 at. % Cr will improve the resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion of TiB2 by 30% compared to undoped TiB2, by acting as a barrier to prevent the reaction between TiB2 and molten aluminum.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Cr-rich oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The Cr-rich oxide layer acts as a barrier to prevent the reaction between TiB2 and molten aluminum, reducing corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion by 30% compared to undoped TiB2
generation.uncertainty: The stability and effectiveness of the Cr-rich oxide layer at high temperatures

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the corrosion resistance of Cr-doped TiB2 with undoped TiB2 in molten aluminum at 700°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Cr-doped TiB2 shows no significant improvement in corrosion resistance compared to undoped TiB2, the hypothesis is falsified
